title: Either acceptation of justification: free by faith; quarreling superfluous
source_text: XLIII. Cum ergo, sive vocabulum justificationis restringatur ad solam a reatu absolutionem, sive etiam ad novae & internae justitiae adeptionem extendatur, aequaliter verum sit nos gratis, per Christi gratiam, fide, non ex operibus, & sine operibus legis justificari: nec etiam, sive hoc, sive illo modo sumamus justificationem, quicquam officiat Apostoli scopo, qui unicus est docere, ad hoc ut simus salutis & justitiae participes, non opus esse legem Mosaicam, & foedus operum, sive legale observare, juxta solemnem clausulam, Fac & vives: sed sufficere ut Christi Evangelio credamus, fide viva, & quae per dilectionem operetur, neque alia ratione homines peccatores, justos coram Deo fieri & reputari posse: cum haec, inquam, ita se habeant, superfluum videtur hac de re litigare, nec est quod propterea cuiquam molesti simus, quod apud Apostolum justificationem sic, vel sic accipiat, quandoquidem in eo vera fides, & sana doctrina nihil periclitatur.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore, whether the vocabulary of justification is restricted to mere absolution from guilt, or is also extended to the obtaining of new and inward righteousness, it is equally true that we are justified freely, through Christ's grace, by faith, not of works, and without works of the law: nor, whether we take justification in this way or that, does anything hinder the Apostle's aim, whose sole aim is to teach that in order that we may be partakers of salvation and righteousness there is no need to observe the Mosaic law and the covenant of works, or legal covenant, according to the solemn clause, Do this and you shall live: but it suffices that we believe the Gospel of Christ with a living faith which works through love, and that in no other way can sinful men become and be reputed just before God: since these things, I say, are so, it seems superfluous to quarrel about this matter, nor is there reason that we should on that account be troublesome to anyone because he takes justification in the Apostle thus or thus, seeing that in that true faith and sound doctrine are in no peril.
pass_b_english: Whether justify = bare acquittal or also inward righteousness, we are still free by faith, not of works/law.
Paul's aim stands either way—living love-working faith, not Do this and live; lexical quarrel is superfluous.

choices.english: Do this and you shall live
choices.why: Legal covenant slogan vs Gospel faith.
